title: Classify dyadic aligned windows of the capped source guard and prove its length bound sharp (no κ)
body:
## Result

Claim type: **scoped proof with an exhaustive finite certificate.** No new κ, no supplier admission, no selected-frontier change. It is not a search failure and not a complete multiplication theorem.

It answers the open question of CubeJerry's merged #6972 (`research/core-production-nonempty`): whether its uniform guard `S >= e(6W+1)`, `L >= 12W+2` can be sharpened on **dyadic aligned sections** (`N = S+e` and `L` powers of two, every window starting at a multiple of `L`). Write `e = 2^j t` with `t` odd, `N = 2^n`, `L = 2^l`, and assume `S >= e(6W+1)`.

1. **Exact classification.** All aligned windows of length `L` have longest selected run `M > 6W` if and only if (I) `l >= n-j+1`; or (II) `l = n-j` and (`t >= 3` or `L >= 12W+2`); or (III) `l <= n-j-1` and `(t+1)L > t(12W+3)`. The odd part `t` of `e` and `n-j` decide, not `S/e`. The source's holes repeat with period `N/2^j`, and in case (III) their offsets modulo `L` are exactly the nearest integers to `L rho/t`.
2. **Single-hole band.** For any window (aligned or not) of length `L >= 6W+1`: bad iff it contains a hole at offset in `[L-1-6W, 6W]`, and such a hole is automatically alone in its window.
3. **The length threshold cannot be lowered on dyadic sections.** For every `W >= 1` and every power of two `L <= 12W` there is a dyadic instance with `S >= e(6W+1)` in which every aligned window of length `L` is bad (`e = N/L`, one hole at offset `L/2`, `M = L/2`). So `L >= 12W+2` is exactly the universal dyadic length condition.
4. **It does sharpen for particular `e`.** For `e` a power of two in case (III), `L >= 6W+2` is necessary and sufficient, half the uniform length. At `W = 1` that is `L = 8` instead of 16; the table of least dyadic `L` per odd part is in the README.
5. **Neither adverse family of #6972 is dyadic** (odd length `12W+1`; odd period `18W+5`). In a dyadic instance `S = e(6W+1)-1` never occurs.

The proofs are in `PROOF.md`, written by hand.

## Evidence

`verify.py` is standard-library only. Its independent oracle is a literal coordinate walk of `q(j) = j + floor(e j/S + 1/2)`.

- Oracle fidelity: the literal walk equals #6972's closed-form longest run on all 72,611 ordinary windows with `S <= 22` (the pinned `guard.py` bytes are hash-checked). This checks my model of `M`; it does not re-check #6972's carve theorem.
- Hole formula, cell lengths and run formula: 400 pairs `(S,e)` with `S >= 2e`, `S <= 40`, 273,910 windows.
- Periodicity of the hole pattern for every `e < N`, `N = 2^n <= 4096`: 8,178 cases.
- Band criterion and the closed form of Theorem 2 against the oracle, every `e` with `N >= 8e`, every `l`, every allowed `W`: 2,070 cases for `N <= 256` (1,415 bad) with the literal walk, and 90,820 cases for `512 <= N <= 4096` (57,364 bad) from the validated hole list. Zero disagreements.
- 1,858 of the latter cases are exactly admissible with `L < 12W+2` (1,260 with `t = 1`, 598 with `t >= 3`).
- Theorem 3's family, checked literally for `W <= 64` (495 families); the parity remark for `W <= 200`.
- Seven wrong variants (threshold `12W+2`; case II merged; `e` in place of its odd part; uniform guard only; case II always admissible; band end shifted by one in each direction) each contradict the oracle in at least one case, so the test domain separates them from the truth.

### Reproduction

From the repository root. Local interpreter: CPython 3.12.15 at `~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12`.

```sh
~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -B research/dyadic-aligned-window-guard/verify.py
~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -B research/dyadic-aligned-window-guard/verify.py
~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/dyadic-aligned-window-guard
~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/dyadic-aligned-window-guard --check-source-history
```

Local results at head `f4314807884fdddd8727a55285ed5442b865306c`: the verifier prints `PASS_DYADIC_ALIGNED_WINDOW_GUARD` in about 6 s (about 9 s with `-O`); the registered runner prints `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE ... outcome=completed` in about 19 s for both commands (each has a 120 s timeout); the commit check prints `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`; the verifier also compiles and runs under `-W error`.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

- Everything is under `S >= e(6W+1)`, i.e. `floor(S/e) >= 6W+1`. Dyadic instances below it are not classified here.
- #6972's equivalence "interior nonempty iff `M > 6W`", its cap and width admissions, source accuracy, the complementary gap `N-L >= W` in applications, and every numerical, compiler and native obligation are cited and untouched.
- The finite check covers `N <= 4096` for the classification and `W <= 64` for the sharpness family; the all-`n` statements rest on the written proofs (Lemma P and Theorems 1 to 3). No proof-kernel check was run and no independent human review is claimed.
- In #6972's own asymptotic family (`L >= p^400`, `W = O(sqrt(p) polylog p)`), `L` already exceeds `12W+2`, so this classification changes nothing there. It decides finite short dyadic sections, and so says exactly which of them are genuinely empty.

## Open next questions

1. Which aligned windows fail in dyadic instances with `floor(S/e) <= 6W`? This is the `S/e` half of the guard. First step: repeat the hole-offset method with internal cells of length `6W` or `6W+1` and test which aligned windows contain no `(6W+1)`-cell. Blocker: those cells form a Sturmian pattern whose offsets modulo `L` need a separate argument.
2. What replaces the periodicity lemma when `N` is not a power of two but `L | N`? First step: for `N = 2^a b` with `b` odd, test whether the holes repeat with period `N/2^j` times a factor of `b`.
3. Can the exact list of empty short aligned sections feed the zero-dimensional branch of #6972's open question 3? First step: take one bad section, for example `W = 1`, `L = 8`, `e = 8`, `N = 64`, through the source, numerical, ownership and cost contracts. Blocker: no native empty-interior service exists in either package.

## Related open work

No open PR studies the capped-carve window guard or cites #6972 (searched titles and bodies of all 431 open PRs for `core-production-nonempty`, nonempty interior, capped carve, `Core.partition`, longest selected run, production Core, and `#6972`).
